stem: A client with type 2 diabetes who takes metformin is scheduled for cardiac catheterization using intra-arterial iodinated contrast. Which action regarding metformin should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Continue metformin through the catheterization and recheck eGFR 48 hours later, withholding subsequent doses if the postprocedure renal function has declined.
options.B: Discontinue metformin at or before the catheterization, re-evaluate eGFR 48 hours later, and restart the medication if renal function is stable.
options.C: Discontinue metformin for the procedure, then resume it later the same day once oral intake returns, arranging renal testing if reduced urine output develops.
options.D: Continue metformin when the preprocedure eGFR is at least 60 mL/min/1.73 m², because intra-arterial contrast alone does not require temporary interruption.

rationale: The current metformin prescribing information directs clinicians to discontinue metformin at the time of or before an iodinated contrast imaging procedure in patients who will receive intra-arterial iodinated contrast. It further directs re-evaluation of eGFR 48 hours after the imaging procedure and restarting metformin if renal function is stable. Current FDA labeling for the iodinated contrast agent ISOVUE gives the same metformin interaction instructions. Therefore B is correct. A incorrectly continues metformin through an intra-arterial contrast procedure. C restarts metformin the same day instead of waiting for the required 48-hour renal-function reassessment. D incorrectly treats a preprocedure eGFR of at least 60 mL/min/1.73 m² as eliminating the intra-arterial-contrast criterion; the label lists intra-arterial contrast as an independent reason for temporary discontinuation.
educational_objective: For a client receiving intra-arterial iodinated contrast, anticipate holding metformin at or before the procedure, re-evaluating eGFR 48 hours afterward, and restarting metformin only if renal function is stable.
source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine — DailyMed
source_document_title: Metformin Hydrochloride Tablets — Full Prescribing Information
source_locator: Full Prescribing Information §2.4 — Discontinuation for Iodinated Contrast Imaging Procedures: discontinue metformin at the time of or prior to iodinated contrast imaging in patients with eGFR 30–60 mL/min/1.73 m², specified comorbid risk factors, or patients who will receive intra-arterial iodinated contrast; re-evaluate eGFR 48 hours after imaging and restart if renal function is stable.
source_claim_supported: Intra-arterial iodinated contrast is itself a labeled criterion for temporary metformin discontinuation at or before the procedure, followed by eGFR reassessment at 48 hours and restart only if renal function is stable.

supporting_sources.locator: §7.1 Drug-Drug Interactions — Metformin: stop metformin at the time of or prior to ISOVUE administration in patients meeting specified renal/comorbidity criteria or receiving intra-arterial iodinated contrast; re-evaluate eGFR 48 hours after imaging and reinstitute metformin only after renal function is stable.
supporting_sources.claim_supported: Current FDA contrast-agent labeling independently confirms the intra-arterial-contrast metformin hold and 48-hour renal-function reassessment rule.

blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p. 38 and related Medication Administration content: review pertinent data prior to medication administration, including contraindications, laboratory results, allergies, and potential interactions; evaluate appropriateness and accuracy of medication orders and educate clients about medications.
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication management around iodinated contrast and renal-function monitoring
correction_summary: Rebuilt the alternatives to remove distractor-only absolute wording and make each option a realistic metformin-management plan. The final item preserves the current label's exact intra-arterial contrast criterion and 48-hour eGFR/restart sequence without converting conditional labeling into a broader universal rule.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Metformin — iodinated contrast interaction and renal-function reassessment
audit_findings.stem: PASS — specifies intra-arterial iodinated contrast, which is an explicit labeling criterion for temporary metformin discontinuation, and does not require an unstated baseline eGFR to identify the correct action.
audit_findings.option_A: PASS as distractor — delayed renal reassessment is appropriate, but continuing metformin through an intra-arterial contrast procedure conflicts with current labeling.
audit_findings.option_B: PASS — exactly follows current DailyMed/FDA labeling: stop at or before the procedure, re-evaluate eGFR after 48 hours, and restart if renal function is stable; uniquely best.
audit_findings.option_C: PASS as distractor — temporary interruption is appropriate, but same-day restart based on oral intake or symptoms bypasses the specified 48-hour eGFR reassessment.
audit_findings.option_D: PASS as distractor — eGFR is relevant to metformin safety, but the labeling lists intra-arterial iodinated contrast as a separate criterion for temporary discontinuation even when the eGFR 30–60 criterion is not met.
audit_findings.ambiguity: PASS — B is the only option that satisfies both the intra-arterial hold criterion and the labeled 48-hour renal-function/restart sequence.
audit_findings.second_answer: EXCLUDED — A and D continue metformin despite the route-specific criterion; C restarts before the required reassessment.
audit_findings.cueing: PASS — all four options are closely matched in length, structure, and clinical specificity; no distractor-only absolute term remains.
audit_findings.blueprint: PASS — NCSBN Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies directly includes review of contraindications, laboratory results, interactions, and medication-order appropriateness.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — challenged whether a normal preprocedure eGFR could justify continuation. Current metformin and FDA contrast-agent labeling independently list intra-arterial iodinated contrast as a criterion for discontinuation at or before imaging and require 48-hour eGFR reassessment before restart, leaving B uniquely correct.
